title: PRD acceptance triage for emergent scope reductions, interlock ledger & signoff path
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Create a decision-ready, low-friction triage process and artifact set for PRD changes that intentionally reduce scope (e.g., cut features, defer prompt-eval work, tighten SLAs) so Eng/Design/Legal can sign off without blocking launch. Context: We've seen multiple late-stage scope reductions where the PRD lacks a compact dependency ledger and explicit legal/ops acceptability criteria. That has led to ambiguous rollbacks and stalled releases. This ticket will produce the interlock ledger template, a condensed signoff matrix, and an escalation path for unresolved items.
out_of_scope: Major re-architecture decisions; new legal policy drafting beyond acceptance criteria; automating the ledger into the Console (follow-up ticket if needed).
decision_points: Which minor scope reductions require formal legal signoff vs. notification
Acceptable risk envelope for deferring telemetry/opt-out clauses
Thresholds for customer-impacted UX changes that mandate design rework
acceptance_criteria: A compact interlock ledger template exists (CSV + one-page narrative) that captures dependency owner, impact level, mitigation, and required signoff role
A 3-step triage flow is documented and linked in the PRD template: (1) PM-led assessment, (2) 48-hour legal/design review window, (3) explicit signoff or documented escalation
Signoff matrix populated with named roles (design lead, eng owner, legal counsel, SRE) and acceptable substitutes for on-call absences
Two example PRDs updated to use the ledger and pass through the new flow in a dry-run; notes captured in decision log
Escalation path documented with SLAs and owner rotation; one on-call escalation flow validated with Support & SRE teams
Security/legal checklist items requiring encryption, data residency, or PII handling are marked and trigger security_review_required = true
path_to_signoff: PM posts PRD change with attached ledger and short diff summary
Design reviews for UX regressions within 48 hours and either approve or request sketches
Engineering assesses implementation risk and rollout controls and responds within 48 hours
Legal reviews any customer/data-facing changes and either signs off or escalates to Legal Manager within 72 hours
If any role declines, PM opens an escalation with the rotation owner; escalation must resolve or schedule a blocking decision meeting within 5 business days
notes: We should favor short, machine-readable ledgers (CSV) plus one-paragraph context to avoid burying decisions in long PRDs.
Legal emphasized that privacy-related deferrals are not acceptable without compensating controls; this is captured in the checklist.
Design asked for a minimal visual diff requirement for any UX removal that touches primary flows (signup, billing, inference output).
